Eperjeske Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Eperjeske, Hungary

Demolished. Eperjeske's Jewish cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map, though it was demolished, likely during or shortly after World War II, and built over by the municipal cemetery. A local Hungarian heritage site records that two Jewish gravestones once existed here, though neither survives today, and a 2020s field survey found only Christian stones, though locals confirmed Jewish gravestones existed there previously. The village's small Jewish population - 32 residents in 1880, peaking at 51 by 1910 - had shrunk to just 6 by 1941. In mid-April 1944, Eperjeske's Jews were confined to the Kisvárda Ghetto and deported to Auschwitz by the end of May; only 2 Jewish residents remained by 1949.
